source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 6 May 1939, p. 6 ("Magherafelt District Council: two contests"); Mid-Ulster Mail, 13 May 1939, p. 5 ("Only one Council contest"); Ballymena Weekly Telegraph, 10 June 1939, p. 2 ("Congratulated"); Ballymena Observer, 9 June 1939, p. 5 ("Portglenone")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Mid-Ulster Mail 6 May 1939 p6 (image read) for the two nominations; Mid-Ulster Mail 13 May 1939 p5 (image read): 'Mrs. O'Kane, the outgoing Councillor for the Clady division, where there had been two nominations, had withdrawn'; the Ballymena papers of 9-10 June 1939 congratulate Mr. Francis A. O'Kane on 'his return, unopposed, to represent the Clady division'.

note: Triennial election, polled Friday 2 June 1939. Twenty-four of the twenty-six divisions were uncontested; Bellaghy was polled; Clady had two nominations but Mrs. A. O'Kane withdrew. Co. Londonderry polled Friday 2 June 1939: 'Polling in the Enagh Lough Division ... took place yesterday' (Londonderry Sentinel, 3 June 1939, p. 8). Re-filed from 1939-05-31, a provisional date (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Two nominations: Mrs. A. O'Kane, the present member, and Mr. F. A. O'Kane; Mrs. O'Kane withdrew, so F. A. O'Kane was returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
